subject.title: [Feature]: Memory durability config — hard flush threshold, priority-aware compaction, cache TTL

question: Should OpenClaw add public config/runtime contracts for hard token memory flush, priority-preserving compaction metadata, and embedding-cache TTL, and which parts should be accepted, redesigned, or rejected?
rationale: The current code lacks the requested keys, but adding them changes public memory durability semantics and overlaps existing force-flush, compaction-provider, and memory-search cache behavior.

options.title: Split The Contracts
options.body: Approve, reject, or redesign hard flush, priority preservation, and TTL independently before implementation so the public config surface stays narrow.

options.title: Accept The Bundle
options.body: Treat the three knobs as one production-memory durability package and require fresh-install, upgrade, and scale proof before merge.

options.title: Defer New Config
options.body: Keep current force-flush and compaction-provider behavior while routing cache TTL or priority preservation to narrower future issues only if maintainers want them.

recommendation.title: Split The Contracts
recommendation.body: Approve, reject, or redesign hard flush, priority preservation, and TTL independently before implementation so the public config surface stays narrow.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest history owner for both memory flush and embedding cache foundations, and the decision spans those surfaces.
